summary: A field for a number you can type or step. Minus and plus sit at the ends of the field, a unit or a currency sign sits beside the value, and a hint under it gives the range. Press and hold minus or plus to keep going, faster the longer you hold; the arrow keys move a step, Shift or Page Up and Page Down ten. A typed value is rounded to the step and kept inside the range when you press Enter or leave the field, and the hint says what changed, like "$20.00 is the most" or "Rounded to 35 steps". The demo sets an agent's run limits.
use: For limits and quantities with a sensible range: an agent's steps, budget and time per run, retries, seats, a page size.
When people often move a value by a step or two, and sometimes type it outright.
Instead of a slider when the exact number matters more than a feel for where it sits in its range.
features: `min`, `max`, `step` and `bigStep` (10 by default) set the range and how far the keys move it; `decimals` sets how the value shows, like 2 for money.
`prefix` and `unit` show beside the value ("$", "steps", "min"); the value and its unit stay centred between minus and plus.
Minus is disabled at `min` and plus at `max`. Pressing and holding either one steps at once, then repeats, faster as you hold.

What you type is checked as you go (anything but digits and a point marks the field in red) and kept on Enter or when you leave: rounded to the step and kept inside the range. Escape puts back the value before.
The hint shows the range ("5 to 100, in steps of 5") or, after a value was changed to fit, what changed. Set your own with `hint`.
`NumberFieldGroup` is the panel from the demo: a title, a line under it, the fields and a summary at the foot.
a11y: The input is a spinbutton with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and the value in words as aria-valuetext ("10 minutes"); it is labelled by the field's label.
Up and Down move a step, Shift with an arrow or Page Up and Page Down move ten. Enter keeps what was typed and Escape puts back the value before.
Minus and plus are named buttons ("Fewer steps", "More steps") left out of the tab order, since the keys do the same; a person using a pointer presses or holds them.
A value that isn't a number is marked with aria-invalid and a red edge, not colour alone: the hint asks for a number in the range.
Clicking the label or beside the value puts the cursor in the field.

faq.q: Why not an input with type="number"?
faq.a: Its spinner is tiny, looks different in every browser, changes the value when you scroll over it, and can't show a unit. This keeps the same keys and the spinbutton role, with buttons you can hit and a unit beside the value.

faq.q: What happens to a value that is out of range?
faq.a: It is kept at the nearest end when you press Enter or leave the field, and the hint says so, like "100 steps is the most". `onValueChange` only ever gets values inside the range and on a step.
Yes. Use `prefix="$"` and `decimals={2}`, with a step like 0.25. For other currencies, change the prefix or use `unit` for a code after the value.
